papers.title: Detecting Tidal Resonances in Binary Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: As a binary neutron star inspirals due to the emission of gravitational waves, the rising tidal frequency resonantly excites vibrational modes. These oscillations are seismological probes of the rich stellar interior, yet it remains to be established whether gravitational-wave interferometers can measure them. Here, we present the first fully Bayesian study of the capability of the Einstein Telescope to detect tidal resonances. We simulate one year of observations and analyse the 200 loudest signals. We find that the Einstein Telescope can identify resonant modes and is sensitive to gravitational-wave phase shifts as small as $ΔΦ\approx 0.03$ for favourable events. We further show that neglecting resonances can bias the inferred tidal deformabilities. These results establish tidal resonances as a measurable route for asteroseismology with future detectors.

ai_review.summary: This paper asks whether the Einstein Telescope could measure neutron-star oscillations excited by tidal resonances during binary inspiral. It simulates a year of observations and performs Bayesian analyses of the 200 loudest signals, comparing models with and without resonant phase evolution. Favorable examples permit phase shifts as small as approximately 0.03 radians to be distinguished, while omitting resonances can bias the recovered tidal deformability. The study goes beyond a Fisher-only sensitivity estimate by examining foreground and background evidence distributions. Its main contribution is a concrete inference forecast for neutron-star asteroseismology. The quoted detection significance remains conditional on the assumed populations, waveform prescriptions and tail calibration; mapping measured resonance parameters into dense-matter constraints is a further step.
ai_review.relevance_reason: A direct match to tidal resonance and gravitational-wave inference, although the sources are neutron-star binaries rather than EMRIs.
ai_review.quality_reason: Bayesian injection/control comparisons provide substantial evidence for the forecast. The claimed high-significance threshold is extrapolated from a small simulated background, making its calibration an important qualification.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, evidence-threshold analysis and conclusion. No independent inference or figure check. A five-sigma threshold is estimated using a density model fitted to 200 background signals; favorable-event sensitivity is not a population-wide guarantee.
ai_review.evidence_quote: constructed from the 200 simulated signals without tidal resonances.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from inclined orbits around Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on generic inclined orbits provide a critical dynamical probe of strong field gravity, as they uniquely break the severe parameter degeneracies inherent to planar equatorial trajectories. To isolate the exact rotational signatures, we extend the periodic-orbit framework to three-dimensional inclined trajectories in the Kerr spacetime, specifically focusing on the $r$--$θ$ orbital resonances. By mapping the geodesic motion into a co-precessing spatial framework parameterized by Mino time, we compute the emitted quadrupole waveforms and evolve the local dynamics using circularity-preserving radiation reaction. It is demonstrated that frame-dragging induces a transient dynamical tilt at periastron, which directly splits the emitted radiation into an exact five-comb spectral architecture. When this resonant structure is resolved over a single coherence time, the statistical error on the dimensionless spin is reduced to $σ_a \approx 10^{-2}$, improving upon the equatorial baseline by up to two orders of magnitude. Because any bound orbit in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime generates a maximum of three frequency combs, the detection of this five-comb hierarchy establishes a rigorous, model-independent null test to strictly exclude spherical geometries.

ai_review.summary: The authors extend a periodic-orbit description of EMRIs to inclined Kerr trajectories with commensurate radial and polar frequencies. They construct quadrupole kludge waveforms in a co-precessing description and study how frame dragging redistributes radiation into five frequency combs. A local radiation-reaction prescription tests whether this structure survives for a coherence interval. Fisher calculations and simulated comparisons suggest that resolved sidebands can improve spin inference relative to selected equatorial examples. The useful result is a connection between three-dimensional orbital structure and potentially informative spectral features. The stronger claim of a model-independent exclusion of spherical geometries should be read within the adopted quadrupole, resonance and signal-comparison framework, rather than as an established null test for arbitrary realistic EMRI waveforms.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Closely matches inclined EMRIs, orbital resonances and Kerr waveform structure, with useful questions for more accurate perturbative modeling.
ai_review.quality_reason: The geodesic-to-spectrum construction, radiation-reaction test and inference examples form a substantive model study. Strong general claims require validation beyond the semi-relativistic kludge and restricted resonant configurations.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusions. Waveforms, Fisher calculations and figures were not reproduced. Five-comb counting and quoted spin errors are conditional on the radiation prescription, resolved coherence interval and selected comparison models.

papers.title: Lasting mEMRIs: Signatures of Multiple Black Hole Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals from AGN discs
papers.abstract: Encounters of stellar-mass black holes (sBH) in active galactic nuclei discs naturally form mean-motion resonances of sBH pairs. These mean-motion resonances can be broken close to the central supermassive black hole when gravitational-wave emission dominates over gas torques. We derive a simple condition that depends only on the sBH mass ratio and the resonance index for which a pair of sBH in a mean-motion resonance will remain intact and can be detectable as a multiple Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals (mEMRIs) in the LISA band. We present for the first time the gravitational-wave strain signatures of a pair of co-migrating sBH in mean-motion resonance, including additional gravitational-wave harmonics associated with orbital conjunctions of the individual EMRIs. The frequency evolution and the associated chirp mass is degenerate with isolated EMRIs of different masses. However, the mEMRI mass ratio is quantised by the resonance order and is larger than the true mass ratio. The degeneracy can be broken if the true sBH mass ratio can be inferred from individual strain amplitudes. We argue that mEMRIs should be common if disc driven EMRIs are to be detected by LISA, with $\sim 10$ mEMRIs per year in the local universe ($z \lesssim 0.2$), highlighting the need to model mEMRI systems in future LISA data analysis.

ai_review.summary: This study follows pairs of stellar-mass black holes captured into mean-motion resonances while migrating through an AGN disc. Few-body simulations coupled to a disc model are combined with an analytic criterion for resonance survival when gravitational radiation overtakes gas torques. Below a resonance-order-dependent mass-ratio threshold, the pair can remain locked and form a multiple EMRI. The resulting strain contains additional harmonics associated with conjunctions, while frequency evolution can mimic isolated systems with different inferred masses. The work identifies possible ways to break this degeneracy and motivates templates for coupled sources. Its event-rate estimates and strong-field survival predictions remain conditional on disc-driven formation, migration prescriptions and the dynamical approximations used in the simulations.
ai_review.relevance_reason: An especially close intersection of EMRIs, environmental effects and resonances, with concrete implications for waveform modeling in AGN discs.
ai_review.quality_reason: An analytic survival criterion is connected to numerical migration experiments and explicit signal consequences. The paper distinguishes resonance-locking behavior from the less certain formation-rate and association problems.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and summary. No independent simulation or figure check. Disc prescriptions and relativistic resonance breaking need further stress tests; identifying and associating both signals requires more complete statistical analyses and waveform templates.
ai_review.evidence_quote: We derived a simple analytic criterion for the stability of these MMRs

papers.title: Polarization-Dependent Photon Propagation, Quasinormal Modes, and Gravitational Lensing in Higher-Curvature Effective Theories
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of higher-curvature corrections on photon propagation within an effective field theory framework and their observational consequences in strong gravitational fields. We consider polarization-dependent modifications to photon trajectories in static and spherically symmetric spacetimes, focusing on Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström black hole backgrounds. Using the geometrical optics approximation, we derive the effective metrics governing photon propagation and study the resulting polarization-dependent shifts of the photon sphere. We compute the corresponding quasinormal modes in the eikonal limit and analyze their polarization dependence. We further investigate gravitational lensing, focusing on polarization-dependent corrections to the deflection angle in both weak- and strong-field regimes. In the strong-deflection regime, we find that even perturbatively small EFT corrections modify the coefficient of the logarithmically divergent part of the deflection angle, resulting in a potentially observable difference from the uncorrected case. This suggests that strong gravitational lensing may provide a sensitive probe of small higher-curvature corrections. While extracting EFT information directly from QNM frequencies is more subtle, QNMs may provide complementary information to gravitational lensing in future studies. Our results establish a framework for probing higher-curvature effects through polarization-dependent strong-field observables.

ai_review.summary: The paper examines how curvature-electromagnetic couplings in an effective theory modify photon propagation around static Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom black holes. In geometrical optics, different polarizations follow different effective metrics, shifting unstable photon orbits and producing gravitational birefringence. The authors derive associated changes to weak- and strong-deflection lensing and discuss frequencies through an eikonal photon-sphere relation. A notable point is that small corrections can alter the coefficient of the logarithmic strong-deflection behavior, not merely shift a ray trajectory. This provides a theoretical framework linking propagation laws and strong-field observables. It does not by itself establish measurable parameter constraints or replace a full wave-equation treatment of finite-multipole gravitational ringdown in a specified higher-curvature theory.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Relevant to gravitational lensing and QNM-related strong-field geometry, with photon-propagation effects rather than an EMRI or self-force calculation at its center.
ai_review.quality_reason: The effective-metric and strong-deflection construction offers a coherent theoretical calculation. Claims about complementary spectroscopy and observability require additional wave-dynamical and inference evidence beyond the eikonal description.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusion/discussion. No independent algebra or figure verification. Results rely on perturbative EFT and geometrical optics in static backgrounds; photon-sphere correspondences should not be treated as complete gravitational-ringdown predictions.
ai_review.evidence_quote: higher-curvature interactions lead to modified dispersion relations and polarization-dependent effective metrics.

papers.title: Chaotic dynamics and resonances in Einstein-Rosen standing wave spacetimes
papers.abstract: Recent work has revealed chaotic geodesic behavior in Einstein-Rosen standing gravitational wave spacetimes. The dynamics of massive test particles are dominated by chaotic heteroclinic networks. This study demonstrates that the dynamical structure of the system is far richer than previously thought. Applying the subharmonic Melnikov function method to Poincaré maps reveals the admissible types of heteroclinic networks. I trace the evolution of these structures under the continuous change of the solution's parameters. In this way, I identify bifurcation phenomena, including a period-doubling bifurcation.

ai_review.summary: This paper investigates geodesic chaos in an Einstein-Rosen standing gravitational-wave spacetime. Rather than classifying trajectories from numerical Poincare plots alone, it applies a subharmonic Melnikov-function analysis to explain which periodic heteroclinic networks can occur. The analysis uncovers structures with different sizes and periodicities and follows their evolution as the solution parameters change. A period-doubling bifurcation supplies an example of how the underlying dynamical organization changes continuously. The contribution is a more explanatory account of resonance and chaos in an exact relativistic wave background. Its immediate setting is a highly symmetric standing-wave model, so the results are principally tools and examples for nonlinear relativistic dynamics rather than predictions for an astrophysical EMRI population or an observed gravitational-wave signal.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Useful for resonance and nonintegrable relativistic dynamics, but more distant from black-hole inspiral modeling than the Kerr and AGN-disc papers.
ai_review.quality_reason: The analytic Melnikov treatment explains structures observed in Poincare maps and connects their allowed periodicities to a parameter-dependent bifurcation study. The claimed result remains appropriately tied to the chosen spacetime.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and summary. The Melnikov calculation and numerical maps were not independently checked. The standing-wave geometry is an idealized dynamical laboratory; transferring its conclusions to inspirals would require a separate calculation.
ai_review.evidence_quote: I explained why only heteroclinic networks of specific periodicity appear in the Poincaré map.

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Diffractive Images Reveal the Structure of Astrophysical Objects
papers.abstract: Scattering patterns encode the structure of extended objects, as demonstrated by charged particle scattering on atomic nuclei. Gravitational wave (GW) diffraction offers an analogous probe of otherwise invisible mass distributions. At linear order in the lens potential we derive expressions relating the central diffractive image contribution to a gravitationally lensed GW waveform to the Fourier transform of the projected lens density. For finite mass lenses this contribution takes the form of a point mass Born amplitude multiplied by a normalized mass form factor, analogous to that in nuclear scattering. As the frequency of GWs from a merging compact binary source evolves the signal samples this form factor across spatial scales, imprinting lens structure through interference with the primary image. Using full numerical wave optics calculations we quantify the observational reach for extended dark matter objects, primordial black holes halo-dressed by dark matter halos and superradiance clouds of ultralight bosons around black holes. For the considered source populations, five year observations with next generation detectors can distinguish extended lenses from point masses, probing dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$, and halo-dressed primordial black holes from matched bare black holes, probing primordial black hole dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-6})$. For sufficiently close source-lens configurations, scalar superradiance clouds can produce distinguishable diffraction signatures for boson masses of approximately $10^{-17}-10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. These results provide a framework for characterizing extended dark matter and compact object astrophysical environments.

ai_review.summary: This study relates gravitational-wave diffraction to the internal mass distribution of an extended lens. At linear order in the lens potential, the central diffractive contribution can be written using a Fourier-space form factor of the projected density, analogous to scattering measurements of extended objects. A chirping source samples different spatial scales through its changing frequency. Full numerical wave-optics calculations then examine extended dark-matter lenses, halo-dressed primordial black holes and bosonic clouds near black holes. The work separates detecting a lens from distinguishing its internal structure after matching simpler lens models. Forecasts suggest potentially useful reach for future detectors, but the quoted abundance sensitivities and cloud signatures depend on source populations, geometry and the adopted reference comparisons.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Strongly connects gravitational lensing, environmental structure and ultralight-field clouds, with a transferable physical interpretation of waveform distortions.
ai_review.quality_reason: A controlled analytic interpretation is complemented by numerical wave-optics benchmarks and explicit distinctions between detection and structural identification. Forecast assumptions and approximation domains are stated rather than hidden.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusion. Numerical calculations and figures were not reproduced. The form-factor interpretation has linear-potential and geometric restrictions; abundance forecasts depend on populations and favorable configurations rather than a demonstrated joint inference.
ai_review.evidence_location: Section 8, Conclusion, discussion of superradiance clouds

papers.title: A superconducting LC resonator in a multi-tesla magnetic field for tabletop kHz gravitational-wave detection
papers.abstract: We present a concept for a superconducting inductance--capacitance (LC) resonator immersed in a magnetic field for gravitational-wave detection in the kHz band. In the long-wavelength limit, a gravitational wave in a static magnetic field induces an oscillating magnetic-field perturbation proportional to the static magnetic field applied to the resonator and to the gravitational-wave strain. We show that a superconducting pickup circuit can convert this perturbation into a flux signal read out by a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-based or quantum-limited amplifier chain. Inspired by resonant-mass detectors, we develop a three-loop coupled-circuit model and derive the equivalent strain-noise spectrum, including thermal noise, SQUID backaction, and measurement imprecision. Prototype measurements demonstrate a quality factor of $Q\simeq 5\times 10^5$, while $Q=10^7$ is considered as a future development target. Under the assumed flux coupling and an idealized quantum-limited SQUID noise model, optimized circuits yield projected strain sensitivities of order $10^{-21}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$ over $100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ bands in the $1$--$20\,\mathrm{kHz}$ range. Increasing the active high-field volume and improving quantum-limited readout could enable further sensitivity gains. This compact, tunable detector concept could complement interferometric gravitational-wave searches and motivate investigations of high-frequency astrophysical sources.

ai_review.summary: The authors propose a compact gravitational-wave detector using a superconducting LC resonator in a strong magnetic field. A coupled three-loop circuit model converts an assumed gravitational-wave-induced flux response into a strain-noise estimate, including thermal noise, SQUID backaction and measurement imprecision. A prototype demonstrates a resonator quality factor near 500,000, while the more ambitious sensitivity projections assume a future quality factor of ten million and idealized readout. Under those assumptions, selected kilohertz bands could reach strain-noise levels around 10^-21 per square-root hertz. This is a detector concept supported by a component measurement, not an operational gravitational-wave sensitivity demonstration. Magnetic noise, mechanical motion, high-field performance and the signal-transfer calibration remain decisive experimental requirements.
ai_review.relevance_reason: A peripheral hardware match through gravitational waves and resonators; less relevant to orbital resonance, perturbation theory and EMRI astrophysics.
ai_review.quality_reason: The circuit/noise model and measured prototype quality factor provide concrete support for a concept study. The full detector sensitivity relies on assumptions that have not yet been experimentally demonstrated.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusion. No experimental data or figure verification. The projected response, high-field quality factor and magnetic/mechanical noise budgets remain to be validated; the prototype does not demonstrate the quoted strain sensitivity.
ai_review.evidence_quote: Q_{d}=Q_{A}=10^{7} remains a future development target

papers.title: Hankel low-rank matrix approximation for gravitational-wave data analysis
papers.abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), will observe vast numbers of overlapping signals. Disentangling these signals from instrumental noise and from one another constitutes a significant data analysis challenge. We explore a denoising technique based on embedding time series into Hankel matrices: a superposition of $n$ (damped) sinusoids corresponds to a matrix of rank $2n$. Thus, the problem of signal extraction is reduced to a structured low-rank approximation problem. Using synthetic data tailored to GW applications, we benchmark three Hankel-based algorithms: ESPRIT, Cadzow iterations, and iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS). Our test scenarios include isolated and multi-component monochromatic signals, the resolution of sources with closely spaced frequencies, and the recovery of black hole quasinormal modes (QNM). All three algorithms achieve near-optimal performance consistent with Fisher matrix bounds, evidenced by an inverse-square scaling of the mismatch with the signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, a proof-of-concept application to numerical relativity waveforms validates the ability of these algorithms to extract QNM frequencies from ringdown signals. Hankel low-rank approximation therefore offers a transparent, computationally efficient avenue for preprocessing GW time series.

ai_review.summary: This paper studies gravitational-wave denoising by embedding a time series into a Hankel matrix, where a small number of sinusoidal components produces low rank. It compares ESPRIT, Cadzow iterations and iteratively reweighted least squares on synthetic single- and multi-source data, frequency-separation tests and a numerical-relativity ringdown example. The benchmarks report near-Fisher mismatch scaling and demonstrate extraction of prominent QNM components, while exposing algorithm-dependent regularization and mode-counting limitations. The method could provide starting points for more expensive Bayesian inference. Its strongest evidence concerns approximately monochromatic or damped signals in stationary white Gaussian noise; realistic chirps, weak sources, nonstationary noise and large crowded LISA populations require additional validation rather than a direct extrapolation of the toy benchmarks.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Relevant to LISA source separation and QNM extraction, offering practical methods alongside the more physics-focused waveform papers.
ai_review.quality_reason: Comparative algorithms, controlled scaling tests and an NR waveform application provide useful benchmarks. The text also reports regularization bias and degradation when fitting too many modes, which helps calibrate the claim.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and discussion. Code, numerics and figures were not reproduced. Benchmarks mainly use stationary white Gaussian noise; whitening, chirping signals and nonstationary noise need further study, and low-SNR components can be missed.

papers.title: Exceptional points and hysteresis in Kerr-Newman quasi-normal modes
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) and eigenstate hysteresis, previously found in Kerr only with an auxiliary scalar field, arise intrinsically in the quasinormal-mode spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. Using a hyperboloidal formulation of the coupled gravito-electromagnetic Teukolsky equations and a Chebyshev pseudospectral method, we compute the $\ell=m=2$ spectrum and locate four EPs at up to $99.974\%$ of extremality, one from a new repulsion. The gaps close as a square root branch point, and quasistatic loops around one or more EPs exchange the coalescing modes, confirming hysteresis.

ai_review.summary: The authors locate exceptional points in the coupled gravitational-electromagnetic QNM spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. A hyperboloidal formulation and Chebyshev pseudospectral calculation track the l=m=2 sector close to extremality. Four candidate degeneracies exhibit square-root gap closing, while quasi-static loops in spin-charge parameter space exchange the coalescing mode branches; enclosing multiple points can produce a larger mode permutation. The contribution is an intrinsic charged-black-hole realization of spectral branch topology without adding an auxiliary scalar field. The reported hysteresis is a property of following mathematical spectral branches. An astrophysical process that executes the required closed adiabatic parameter cycle remains an open problem, and the located points involve charges unlikely for astrophysical black holes.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Central to quasinormal modes and coupled black-hole perturbation theory, with interesting non-Hermitian spectral structure even if direct astrophysical applications are limited.
ai_review.quality_reason: Gap scaling and mode permutations around parameter loops give complementary diagnostics of the branch-point interpretation. The study distinguishes spectral topology from the unresolved problem of physically realizing a closed cycle.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, spectral-location discussion and conclusions. No independent eigenvalue, resolution or figure check. Near-extremal numerics deserve scrutiny; results concern one multipole sector and require astrophysically large charges.
ai_review.evidence_quote: the square-root closing of the repulsion gaps

papers.title: Untangling Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals and Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA Data
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe sources in the millihertz regime, such as Galactic Binaries (GBs), Massive Black Hole Binaries (MBHBs), and Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), so its data stream will be a superposition of an unknown number of gravitational-wave sources. We consider the joint inference of various representative combinations of MBHB and EMRI signals in LISA data (with assumed instrumental noise and stochastic GB foreground). Our Bayesian analyses confirm the expectation of weak inter-source coupling between EMRIs, and between EMRIs and MBHBs, despite strong intra-source parameter correlations. Weak EMRI-MBHB coupling enables a hierarchically sequential approach to EMRI and MBHB inference, rather than fully joint inference. We further show that imperfect MBHB subtraction, arising from missing modes or overlapping MBHBs, has only a weak impact on EMRI inference. For multiple MBHBs, we mitigate inference errors through a joint MBHB fit. We demonstrate this strategy on simulated LISA data containing noise, three MBHBs, and three EMRIs, jointly fitting and subtracting the MBHBs before sequentially inferring the EMRIs - ultimately observing little to no bias on all recovered astrophysical parameters. The notions described throughout our work are highly relevant to informing optimal strategies for the global-fit-based pipelines that are currently being developed for LISA.

ai_review.summary: This paper tests a practical hierarchy for inference in LISA data containing EMRIs and massive black-hole binaries. Bayesian analyses of representative mixtures find weak correlations between different EMRIs and between EMRIs and MBHBs, even when parameters within each source remain strongly correlated. The proposed strategy fits and subtracts MBHBs first, treating nearby mergers jointly, then infers the EMRIs sequentially. A simulated data stream with three sources of each type demonstrates this procedure without requiring a fully joint six-source fit. Tests also examine imperfect subtraction from omitted MBHB modes. The result supports an efficient proof-of-principle workflow for the studied configurations, while broader populations, realistic white-dwarf sources and more complex data artifacts remain necessary stress tests.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Directly relevant to EMRI waveform inference and LISA analysis, with a concrete strategy for separating sources and controlling subtraction errors.
ai_review.quality_reason: Joint-versus-sequential inference comparisons, overlapping-source cases and missing-mode experiments substantiate the proposed hierarchy. The paper explicitly limits generalization beyond its representative simulated configurations.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusion. Inference runs and figures were not reproduced. Weak inter-source coupling is not established for arbitrary populations; a stochastic confusion foreground does not replace fully modeling resolved white-dwarf sources.
ai_review.evidence_quote: proof-of-principle study rather than a population-level analysis

papers.title: Curvature Reconstruction and Tensor Polarizations in Isospectrality-Breaking Black-Hole Perturbations
papers.abstract: Testing general relativity with the ringdown phase of gravitational waves requires connecting modifications of black-hole perturbation dynamics to observable signatures in detector strain. In this work, we study the relation between curvature perturbations, metric master variables, and detector tensor polarizations for nonrotating black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. In this theory the axial gravitational perturbation couples to a dynamical scalar field, while the polar sector remains GR-like at the order considered. We first construct a map for the perturbed Weyl scalar $δΨ_0$, expressing its even-parity part in terms of the ZM master function and its odd-parity part in terms of the RW master function together with the scalar radial perturbation. We also derive the leading asymptotic tensor polarizations $h_+$ and $h_\times$ directly from the metric perturbations. The resulting strain is reconstructed from the radiative gravitational master functions: the ZM function in the even sector and the Cunningham-Price-Moncrief-normalized odd function in the axial sector for dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. No independent local algebraic term proportional to the scalar radial function appears in the leading tensor strain. These results separate curvature-level scalar dependence from tensor-channel scalar-frequency responses and provide the formal reconstruction basis for companion work on parity-split beating and effective ringdown frequencies.

papers.title: Joint Angular-Power Distributions of Interfering Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. We characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged Earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved Legendre coefficients. A hybrid model of bright sources and a Gaussian faint background extends the conditional Gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $χ^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. Our analytical variance decomposition and SMBHB population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. In the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. These results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.

papers.title: Tracking the Evolution of Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with Pulsar Terms
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays will soon be able to resolve the loudest supermassive black hole binaries contributing to the stochastic gravitational wave background at nanohertz frequencies. While the few decades of observations are typically not enough to see these binaries evolve in frequency, the so-called pulsar terms offer a glimpse into the past and can help us map out the frequency evolution of these binaries over tens of thousands of years. Measuring this long-term frequency evolution can allow us to look for deviations from a vacuum binary evolution due to various environmental effects. We develop a Fisher-matrix approach to calculate how precisely the frequency can be tracked over time in this manner, and demonstrate its use on a realistic near-future pulsar timing array with a 30-year baseline. We find that the environmental effects predicted by 2-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of circumbinary disks are unlikely to be detectable in the circular binaries we considered, however, in some cases they might result in biased chirp mass recovery if ignored. We also demonstrate how this approach allows one to test the orbital evolution predicted by general relativity in a purely gravitational-wave driven inspiral, and to put upper limits on additional generic environmental effects described by a power-law hardening model.

papers.title: Higher Dimensional Loop Quantum Black hole in de Sitter Spacetime: Quasinormal Modes and Shadow Signatures
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamical and optical properties of a higher-dimensional loop-quantum-corrected black hole in a de Sitter background. We first analyze the horizon structure and identify the admissible nonextremal black-hole domain bounded by the extremal and Nariai configurations, ensuring the existence of distinct inner, event, and cosmological horizons for the parameter sets considered. We then examine the scalar effective potential and show that the loop-quantum correction deforms the classical scattering barrier primarily in the strong-field region while preserving its characteristic single-barrier structure. The quasinormal modes of massless scalar perturbations are computed using time-domain evolution with Prony extraction, the matrix method, and the WKB approximation, showing good agreement among the three approaches. The time-domain waveform and its Prony and matrix-frequency reconstructions provide an additional direct consistency check of the extracted ringdown spectrum. We find that loop quantum corrections induce moderate shifts in the quasinormal spectrum, whereas the spacetime dimensionality has a much stronger impact, leading to higher oscillation frequencies and damping rates. The negative imaginary parts of all modes indicate dynamical stability against massless scalar perturbations within the explored parameter range. Comparison with the corresponding classical black-hole backgrounds shows that the quantum-corrected quasinormal spectrum remains continuously connected to the classical photon-sphere branch, with the loop correction producing quantitative rather than qualitative changes.

papers.title: The fate of primordial gravitational waves during domain-wall domination
papers.abstract: Primordial gravitational waves probe inflation, but their interpretation depends on their subsequent evolution. During domain-wall domination, a frozen wall network retains a nonzero shear response that can modify the superhorizon evolution of primordial gravitational waves. Starting from the wall-forming scalar field, we derive an effective tensor mass term and a source associated with the frozen wall geometry in the thin-wall, quasistatic limit. Together they drive superhorizon tensor perturbations toward a configuration set by the network. This configuration carries both any inherited primordial deformation and the network's intrinsic random structure. We derive how these contributions enter the tensor transfer and power spectrum. The resulting description connects superhorizon tensor evolution to the microscopic wall response and the geometry established as the network freezes.

papers.title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
papers.abstract: Cross-correlations of galaxies and gravitational waves (GW) can be used to extract cosmological parameters and the gravitational wave bias. In this work, we study how to include galaxy luminosities in these spatial cross-correlations, inspired by the standard approach of dark sirens line-of-sight redshift priors. We present a formalism to include luminosity information in galaxy-GW simulations and study the effects of assigning a hosting probability that depends on luminosity through a simple power law $p_{\rm{host}} \propto L^β$ with $β\in \{0,1,2\}$ corresponding to uniformly, linear and quadratically weighted in luminosity. This effectively changes the GW linear bias with respect to dark matter and, in principle, allows to gain signal-to-noise and a sharper measurement of cosmological parameters. For a realistic luminosity dependence of the galaxy bias taken from DESI data, the gain is marginal, making the method robust to different luminosity weighting prescriptions. We show that the cross-correlation inference is able to recover the injected GW bias within $10\%$ if there is a mismatch between the injected linear bias of host galaxies and observed galaxies, provided that one sticks to relatively large scales. We also show that the Hubble constant and matter energy density can be recovered to $0.5\%$ and $5\%$ respectively with a third generation network of GW detectors, regardless of the modeling of the GW bias.

papers.title: Exploring Exact Einsteinian Black Hole Physics in Dark Matter Environment: Ray Tracing, Stability, Eikonal QNMs and Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent rebuttal of black hole--dark matter solutions based on velocity-matching, we reconstruct the spacetime by treating the dark matter halo density directly as an energy-density source in the Einstein field equations. We obtain an exact static, spherically symmetric black hole solution and investigate the effects of the halo on its geometry, optical properties, quasinormal modes, and thermodynamics. Using null geodesics, we show that the halo modifies photon trajectories, shifts the circular photon orbit, and enlarges the photon sphere and apparent shadow. The Lyapunov exponent of the unstable null orbit further determines the eikonal quasinormal modes, yielding explicit halo-induced corrections to their oscillation and damping rates. We also compute the mass, Hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, and Gibbs free energy to characterize the thermodynamic stability and phase structure. We find that the dark matter halo enlarges the domain of thermodynamic stability and introduces nontrivial phase behavior absent in the Schwarzschild case, demonstrating that astrophysical dark matter environments can leave potentially observable imprints on black hole observables.

papers.title: Spin the black circle II: tidal heating and torquing of a rotating black hole by a test mass on generic orbits
papers.abstract: Horizon fluxes of energy and angular momentum are a key strong-field effect in the dynamics of black holes, encoding direct information about their nature. In this work, we present a numerical study of these fluxes for a test particle orbiting a Kerr black hole on equatorial geodesics, covering circular, eccentric, and hyperbolic trajectories across a wide range of orbital parameters and black hole spins. We reproduce known results for circular orbits and uncover a richer phenomenology for eccentric and hyperbolic ones: the instantaneous fluxes can exhibit multiple peaks and sign changes, indicating a complex interplay between orbital dynamics and horizon perturbation. We then compare these results against existing analytical post-Newtonian expressions, exploring resummation strategies to improve their performance against numerical data. In particular, we propose a factorized and resummed representation of the horizon fluxes that predicts the onset frequency of the superradiant regime to within $10\%$ for $\gtrsim 83\%$ for both the energy and angular momentum fluxes of bound configurations; high-energy open orbits however remain a challenge. This representation exactly reduces to the circular limit by construction, independently of the perturbative order of the remaining analytical terms. For peak and orbit-averaged fluxes, the analytical models achieve acceptable accuracy -- with relative errors at the $10\%$ level or below -- at large separations and low eccentricities. However, they can exhibit deviations of $\sim \mathcal{O}(100\%)$ in the strong-field regime, motivating the need for improved flux prescriptions and further investigations.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Detector for Postmerger Neutron Stars: Beyond the Quantum Loss Limit of the Fabry-Perot-Michelson Interferometer
papers.abstract: Advanced gravitational-wave detectors that have made groundbreaking discoveries are Michelson interferometers with resonating optical cavities as their arms. As light travels at finite speed, these cavities are optimal for enhancing signals at frequencies below their bandwidth frequency. A small amount of optical loss will, however, significantly impact the high-frequency signals which are not optimally amplified. We find an elegant interferometer configuration with an "L-resonator" as the core, significantly surpassing the loss limited sensitivity of dual recycled Fabry Perot Michelson interferometers at high frequencies. Following this concept, we provide a broadband design of a 25 km detector with outstanding sensitivity between 2-4 kHz. We have performed Monte-Carlo population studies of binary neutron star mergers, given the most recent merger rate from the GWTC-3 catalog and several representative neutron star equations of state. We find that the new interferometer configuration significantly outperforms other third-generation detectors by a factor of 3 to 7 in the signal-to-noise ratio of the post-merger signal. Assuming a detection threshold with signal-to-noise ratio >5 and for the cases we have explored, the new design is the only detector that confidently achieves a detection rate larger than one per year, with the rate being 1 to 30 events per year.

papers.title: Grey-body factor from correspondence with quasinormal mode for gravitational perturbation of higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black hole
papers.abstract: We study the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and grey-body factors (GBFs) of higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordström black holes. Considering scalar, vector, and tensor gravitational perturbations, we systematically compute the QNMs and GBFs for each spacetime dimension and set of black-hole parameters to evaluate the analytical formula connecting them. QNMs are obtained by the continued fraction and the integration-through-midpoints methods depending on the singularity structure in the Frobenius series. We compare the GBFs determined by the correspondence using QNMs with those computed numerically. The correspondence performs well for scalar($+$), vector($+$), vector($-$), and tensor perturbations. For the scalar($-$) perturbation, the GBFs obtained by the correspondence deviate noticeably from the accurate GBFs for black holes with low to intermediate values of the charge in $D>6$. The correspondence recovers reasonable accuracy at higher charges, although the effective potential exhibits double peaks, contrary to the assumption underlying the Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB)-based derivation of the correspondence. Whereas the accuracy decreases with increasing $D$ for other perturbation types, the correspondence for the scalar($-$) perturbation yields more accurate GBFs in $D=8$ than those in $D=7$. For near-extreme black holes, the correspondence offers a reliable approximation of GBFs for the vector($-$) perturbation, even though a double-peak potential occurs in $D>6$. These results suggest that the correspondence has a wider range of applicability than might be expected from the assumption of the WKB approach.

papers.title: Exact WKB analysis of inverted triple-well: resonance, PT-symmetry breaking, and resurgence
papers.abstract: We study non-Hermitian quantum mechanics of an inverted triple-well potential within the exact WKB framework. For a single classical potential, different Siegert boundary conditions define three distinct quantum problems: the PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems. For each case, we derive the exact quantization condition and construct the associated trans-series solution. By identifying the resurgent structures and cancellations in these non-Hermitian setups, we obtain the median-summed series, clarifying when the spectra are real or complex in accordance with the physical properties of each system. Establishing explicit links to the semi-classical path integral formalism, we elucidate the roles of bounce and bion configurations in these non-Hermitian systems. This analysis predicts PT-symmetry breaking, which we also verify numerically. Using the median quantization conditions, we prove the existence of this symmetry breaking and establish an exact equation for the exceptional point, which emerges as a remarkably simple algebraic relation between the bounce and bion actions. We further show that the median-summed non-perturbative correction to the spectrum vanishes at the exceptional point, while the resurgent structure survives through a universal minimal trans-series. For the resonance and anti-resonance systems, we find that the exact median-summed spectra are related by complex conjugation, representing time reversal in this setting, are necessarily complex, and do not exhibit an exceptional point. Although their spectra differ significantly from the PT-symmetric case, they share the same minimal trans-series. By maintaining explicit links with the path integral saddles and the formal theory of resurgence, our analysis provides a unified and general perspective on the quantization of non-Hermitian theories.

papers.title: In Search of the Gravitational Wave of Fast X-Ray Transient in the Second Part of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Fourth Observing Run
papers.abstract: Fast X-ray Transients (FXTs) are brief, intense X-ray flashes unassociated with persistent X-ray sources or known stellar objects, typically lasting from seconds to hours. With the launch of the Einstein Probe in January 2024, the study of FXTs has entered a new phase. Its large field of view significantly increases the discovery rate, enabling more robust statistics. The leading discoveries have revealed a fraction of gamma-ray bursts, while the rest remain unexplained. We propose a methodology to search for possible relations between gravitational waves (GWs) and FXTs, as it may serve as a discrepancy among proposed theoretical models. To achieve this, we intend to utilize X-Pipeline, an unmodeled search algorithm, to identify excess coherent signals in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) O4b observations. Out of 64 FXTs events, we obtained 19 FXTs for constructing robust searches. Given the absence of any detectable GW signals, we subsequently calculated upper limits and estimated exclusion distances for each source. In order to enrich the sample base and statistical analysis, this methodology could henceforth be conducted through future GW searches, including KAGRA in the O4c and O5 observations.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from highly charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
papers.abstract: We perform fully nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations of electrically charged binary black hole mergers in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMD) theory, varying the magnitude and relative sign of the input charges and the dilaton coupling $a$. In the weak-charge sequence, the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to the neutral vacuum baseline of general relativity and are visually indistinguishable across the sampled couplings, consistent with earlier EMD simulations. For the highly charged binaries with equal-magnitude opposite charges, however, the dominant gravitational strain exhibits visible differences between the EMD cases with $a\neq0$ and the charged Einstein-Maxwell reference at $a=0$. At $a=1$, the coordinate-time interval from the same separation to the waveform-based merger is approximately $62\%$ shorter than for the neutral binary. In this high-charge sequence at fixed input charges, increasing $a$ strengthens the scalar dressing while leaving the individual dilaton-weighted horizon charges nearly unchanged. Within the same sequence, increasing $a$ across the sampled values decreases the dipolar electromagnetic-flux peak, increases the scalar-flux peak, and modestly lengthens the merger interval. The sampled like-charged binaries have corresponding merger intervals approximately $15\%$-$20\%$ longer than the neutral baseline and emit predominantly quadrupolar electromagnetic radiation. At $a=1$ and $a=\sqrt{3}$, the like-charged mergers leave charged remnants with scalar fields consistent with secondary dilaton hair. The opposite-charge remnants instead approach neutral black holes without stationary scalar hair.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of Type I perturbations of dilaton-Euler-Heisenberg black holes
papers.abstract: We study the type I quasinormal modes (QNMs) of magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg (dEH) black holes, where axial gravitational and polar electromagnetic perturbations are coupled. Direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods give consistent QNM frequencies for the fundamental branches continued from Schwarzschild at $\ell=1,2,3$. Varying $α$ at fixed $ζ=α-β$ changes the spectrum on the same background. The damping response depends on charge and multipole and can have opposite signs for the two coupled branches. For $ζ<0$, dipole damping decreases with charge toward horizon merger. For $ζ>0$, the Type I charge range extends beyond the complementary polarization's local angular-gradient bound. All tracked modes remain damped in the nonextremal ranges, supporting the stability of these branches.

papers.title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant. Within a standard-siren framework, we perform a joint cosmological and population analysis using $\mathcal{O}(150)$ mock GW detections with SNR > 12, as projected for one year of observations at LVK O5 sensitivity. We combine these with mock HI intensity maps from MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, and study how observational limitations in both the GW and IM data affect the $H_0$ constraints. We find that uncertainty in GW parameter measurements is a dominant limitation on the cosmological constraints. Neglecting this uncertainty, the inclusion of HI information enables sub-percent constraints on $H_0$. We also find that observational effects in the HI surveys weaken the constraints, although they remain tighter than those obtained without HI information (spectral sirens). Despite accounting for HI IM observational limitations, including HI information reduces the $H_0$ uncertainty relative to the spectral-siren results by 61% for MeerKLASS and 53% for SKA-Mid. Because our results are based on a single realisation, they should be interpreted in light of possible realisation-to-realisation variability. Beam convolution most severely weakens the constraints. Instrumental noise can induce multimodality in the posterior, potentially biasing the inferred parameters. The results are sensitive to foreground under-cleaning and over-cleaning. Partial sky coverage has a relatively small impact. In the most realistic scenario, which accounts for both GW and HI IM limitations, we obtain $H_0$ precision estimates of 10% and 15% for MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, respectively.

papers.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
papers.abstract: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.

papers.title: Modeling QNMs-Filtered Gravitational Waveforms: Approximation Limits and Filtering Effects
papers.abstract: The waveform left after quasinormal modes filtering of binary gravitational waveforms, often called the direct wave, has recently attracted considerable debate. Analytic models of this residual waveform involve several levels of approximation, while the effects of filtering on the modeling remain unclear. These issues require further investigation. In this paper, we examine the approximation errors, limits of applicability, and role of filtering in these models. We find that the point-particle models examined here show notable discrepancies with the filtered Binary-black-hole waveforms. Analytic particle templates based on the stationary-phase approximation perform reasonably well for the \((\ell,m)=(2,2)\) multipole, but exhibit substantial limitations for the \((4,4)\). Although the filter is all-pass, it substantially affects the modeling results. Our analytic calculations on a Schwarzschild background further show that vacuum perturbations with Gaussian initial data can also exhibit direct-wave-like waveforms after filtering, with their morphology depending on the location of the initial data relative to the light ring.

papers.title: Axial Perturbations of Extended Tolman III in the New $f(R,T)$ Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate compact objects using the extended Tolman III equation of state in the framework of $f(R,T)=R+2χT$ gravity. In the matter sector of the Lagrangian density, we employ a new formalism based on the evaluation of the second-order derivative of the matter Lagrangian with respect to the metric \cite{Jayawiguna:2026das}. We analyze the corresponding observational signatures through axial gravitational perturbations including stellar stability and gravitational echo. We find that the effective potential in $f(R,T)$ gravity is wider and deeper than its counterpart in general relativity (GR). The quasinormal-mode (QNM) frequencies are calculated using the Bohr--Sommerfeld (BS) fitting and both the lower- and higher-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB) approximations. For the ultracompact configurations considered, trapped modes can tunnel through the potential barrier, giving rise to gravitational-wave echoes. The imaginary parts of the QNM frequencies are found to be negative, $\Im(ω_n M)<0$, indicating that the perturbations decay exponentially with time. Our results show that the echo train in GR contains more echoes than that in $f(R,T)$ gravity. Finally, assuming that the stellar object is a neutron star and adopting a stellar radius consistent with measurements by the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), we find that the $f(R,T)$ gravity model yields a characteristic frequency consistent with the estimated frequency associated with GW170817 for $β= 4.663\times10^{-1}$ and $χ=0.96π$, whereas the corresponding GR model does not exhibit comparable agreement.

papers.title: Pseudo-spectral methods in gravitational lensing: Spin precession in loop quantum black hole spacetimes
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing is usually treated as an initial value problem: for a given impact parameter of an unbound orbit, one computes the resulting deflection angle. In this paper we advocate the inverse point of view. For a prescribed deflection angle, the orbit is selected by two boundary conditions at spatial infinity, so that the lensing problem becomes a well-defined two-point boundary value problem, with the impact parameter playing the role of a nonlinear eigenvalue. We show that pseudo-spectral methods based on Chebyshev collocation solve this boundary value problem accurately at modest computational cost, and that the parallel transport equations governing the spin precession of the particle reduce to a single linear system on the same grid. As a concrete application, we compute the spin precession of massive particles in backward scattering off two black hole spacetimes from loop quantum gravity, the covariant effective metric and the self-dual loop quantum black hole. We find that the quantum corrections are most pronounced for slowly moving particles, while in the ultra-relativistic limit the universal spin flip is always recovered. The flip itself is universal, but the rate at which it is approached is not. The derivative of $\cosξ$ with respect to the particle speed at $v=1$ depends on the quantum parameters of both spacetimes. The framework is not restricted to the models studied here and applies to any static, spherically symmetric spacetime.

papers.title: Crowdsourcing Gravitational Waves from Superradiant Axions
papers.abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of ultralight axions. If nature contains a boson with a mass of order $10^{-12}\,$eV, $\textit{mere vacuum fluctuations}$ will lead to its efficient production around spinning stellar mass black holes, forming a gravitational atom that both drains the black hole spin and decays to produce near-monochromatic gravitational waves. Existing superradiance constraints derive primarily from spin measurements of a handful of identified black holes. Here we instead present a detailed study of the population level effect: gravitational waves arising from both the 100 million black holes in the Milky Way and the stochastic signal from axion clouds throughout the universe. We study the impact of a broad range of systematic uncertainties on the black hole properties and compute the projected axion sensitivity for LIGO, as well as the future instruments Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer, and a high-frequency Magnetic Weber Bar. We demonstrate that LIGO can robustly probe axion masses from roughly $10^{-13}\,$eV to $4 \times 10^{-12}\,$eV. If the black hole population extends to masses slightly below $5\,M_{\odot}$ - as hinted for by LIGO inspiral observations - LIGO would approach $10^{-11}\,$eV. Under that same assumption we show that a future high-frequency detector could push considerably higher, potentially beyond $10^{-10}\,$eV in the most optimistic scenarios, reaching towards the lowest masses within the projected sensitivity of axion dark matter searches.

papers.title: Automated identification and subtraction of gravitational-wave glitches using boundary refinement
papers.abstract: Transient noise artifacts, or glitches, in gravitational wave strain data elevate the false alarm rate of astrophysical searches and degrade parameter estimation when overlapping a signal. No method previously identified a glitch's time boundary: existing detection and classification tools flag and label glitches without resolving their extent, forcing subtraction to run over padded windows that cost time and erase signal beyond the glitch itself. We present three boundary identification methods, AMPS (Amplitude-based Multi-glitch Pulse Segmenter), FLARE (Fitness-based Localization And Refinement Extractor), and CRISP (connected-region identification via spectrogram power), paired with three subtraction techniques, adaptive spline fitting, wavelet shrinkage, and their combination, across five glitches from the GravitySpy database spanning Advanced LIGO's first three observing runs. AMPS sets a boundary from a robust amplitude threshold, FLARE from the best fitness of a segmented spline fit, and CRISP from spectrogram power. Injecting a chirp signal on four broadband glitches, the combined technique recovers 95 to 97 percent of the injected signal-to-noise ratio, against roughly 64 percent for wavelet shrinkage alone. CRISP gives the most uniform boundary width across glitches; AMPS and CRISP both identify a boundary in a fraction of a second, two to three orders of magnitude faster than FLARE. For the glitch overlapping GW170817, a low-frequency residual persists under the default boundary, a deliberate tradeoff against removing signal power. Scattered light glitches remain untested and are the primary direction for future work.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves From an Entangled SO(3) Cosmic String Network
papers.abstract: Discrete non-Abelian symmetries such as $\mathrm{A_4}$ are widely used in models of lepton flavor to explain neutrino mass hierarchy and their large mixing. If such a symmetry arises from the spontaneous breaking of a continuous group, cosmic strings can form. We study the breaking $\mathrm{SO}(3)\to \mathrm{A_4}$, for which the strings are classified by the non-Abelian group $π_1(\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{A_4})\cong \mathrm{T}'$, the binary tetrahedral group. Because the string fluxes do not commute, colliding strings may reconnect, pass through each other, or become joined by a bridge whose flux can belong to a different string network. We derive the probabilities of these outcomes directly from the group structure; in network models they are usually treated as free parameters. Including them in a multi-network velocity-dependent one-scale model, we find that the correlation length of the networks decreases and their energy density increases relative to Abelian $\mathrm{U}(1)$ strings of the same tension. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background is enhanced by up to nearly three orders of magnitude, showing that the algebraic structure of $π_1$ leaves a direct imprint on the gravitational-wave spectrum.

papers.title: Black Hole Shadows and Quasinormal Modes with Dark Matter at the Horizon
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the effect of a surrounding dark matter halo on two horizon-scale observables of a black hole: its shadow and quasinormal-mode spectrum. We consider a Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a Hernquist halo and construct a one-parameter family of solutions that preserve the total halo mass while varying how the halo density vanishes at the horizon. By closing the Einstein equations with an Einstein-cluster stress tensor, we show that horizon regularity requires the density to vanish at least linearly. Our results also indicate that the dominant energy condition is violated in a thin layer outside the horizon, highlighting the limitations of the Einstein-cluster description within the photon sphere. We demonstrate that, at fixed black hole mass, the halo always enlarges the shadow, with the effect becoming more pronounced for more massive and compact halos. Comparison with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr\,A$^*$ and M87$^*$ shows that only sufficiently compact halos can be constrained, with the inferred bounds depending sensitively on whether the observed mass is identified with the black hole mass or the total mass of the system. We further show that the halo lowers both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of electromagnetic and axial gravitational quasinormal modes, leading to higher quality factors. These spectral shifts are quantitatively explained by changes in the photon-sphere properties through the eikonal correspondence. Since the effects scale with the ratio of the halo mass to its size, they are observable only for dark matter concentrated within a few tens of gravitational radii of the black hole, which is the regime considered here.

papers.title: Amplified EFT corrections near exceptional QNMs
papers.abstract: We show that the ordinary expansion of EFT corrections to individual QNM frequencies breaks down at an exceptional QNM, and that these corrections become enhanced for near-exceptional QNMs. We give a brief argument for why this should generally happen, before numerically demonstrating this behaviour by calculating the $α'^3$ corrections to QNMs of equal-spin Myers--Perry-AdS$_5$ black holes. This calculation corresponds to $λ^{-3/2}$ corrections to the poles of the retarded Green's function in the boundary CFT, where $λ$ is the 't Hooft coupling. Treating the coalescing pair together, we calculate the leading $λ^{-3/4}$ splitting at the uncorrected exceptional point and the $λ^{-3/2}$ displacement of the exceptional point in temperature and angular velocity. The background derivative expansion can remain valid while the nondegenerate expansion of individual frequencies fails. We discuss the implications for the full response and for other areas of black hole physics.

papers.title: Calculating gravitational waves at infinity: the missing link
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave science requires waveform templates to be computed at future null infinity, the asymptotic boundary of spacetime. Numerical solutions of Einstein's equations typically rely on a Cauchy evolution on a finite computational domain, but can produce waveforms at infinity by performing a subsequent characteristic evolution that compactifies the spacetime. Such waveforms capture expected physical effects, like gravitational-wave memory and late-time, power-law tails. But this characteristic evolution requires initial data consistent with the interior Cauchy solution to avoid producing spurious, long-lived transients. A careful analysis shows that previous prescriptions for this initial data were not sufficiently consistent and provides a way to remedy the problem. The new initial data yield accurate waveforms from the first cycle onward. The construction is independent of the Cauchy formulation and enables the production of catalogs of robust waveforms at infinity.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from New Inflation
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves provide one of the most powerful observational probes for discriminating among inflationary models. In particular, it has recently become clear that the high-frequency gravitational-wave spectrum encodes a wealth of information about the properties of the inflaton and the post-inflationary dynamics. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive prediction of the complete gravitational-wave spectrum in the new inflation scenario, a prototypical realization of small-field inflation, incorporating all known production mechanisms including both the classical and quantum sources.

papers.title: Deep Learning Search for Gravitational Waves from Compact Binary Coalescence
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave searches rely on a combination of methods, including matched filtering, coherent analyses, and more recent machine-learning-based pipelines. For compact binary coalescences --- where signals originate from the relativistic dynamics of compact objects --- matched filtering remains a central element, but its computational cost will increase substantially with the data volumes and parameter-space coverage required by next-generation interferometers such as the Einstein Telescope. Developing complementary strategies that reduce computational load while preserving detection performance is therefore essential. We investigate a hybrid approach that combines matched-filtering concepts with Convolutional Neural Networks, enabling efficient signal searches without relying on the usual $χ^2$ rejection test. Using simulated data sets that include injected signals in Gaussian noise, transient noise, and physical effects not represented in the template bank --- such as eccentricity, precession and higher-order modes --- we show that the method achieves a detection efficiency comparable to or better than a standard matched-filtering search while offering a more resource-efficient pipeline in all the cases where the physics included in the signals were not represented in the template bank or when glitches were affecting the data. Conversely, the analysis also reveals some loss of detection capability for standard BNS/BBH searches in pure Gaussian noise. These results indicate that deep-learning-assisted searches can support sustainable gravitational-wave data analysis in future detector eras.

papers.title: Cosmological Gravitational Wave Collider Physics
papers.abstract: Primordial tensor non-Gaussianity can probe massive particles present during inflation. We investigate this possibility in an effective field theory where the massless graviton mixes with the helicity-two mode of an additional massive spin-two field $σ_{ij}$ with cubic self-interactions. For constant sound speed, we compute the leading tensor power-spectrum correction and the tree-level bispectrum, finding novel analytical expressions for these quantities. In the $m_σ>3H/2$ regime, we find a nonanalytic squeezed contribution that exhibits logarithmic oscillations with characteristic dependence $(k_L/k_S)^{3/2\pm iμ}$, where $μ=\sqrt{m_σ^2/H^2-9/4}$. The oscillation frequency is set by the mass $m_σ$, while the polarisation contractions determine the relative amplitudes of the different graviton helicity configurations. The same mixing generates corrections to the power spectrum and the bispectrum. We derive the associated quadrupolar modulation of short-scale tensor power spectrum and relate its amplitude to the model parameters. Finally, we explore how a slowly varying sound speed modifies the squeezed signal.~These results connect the two-point, three-point, and quadrupolar tensor signatures of massive spin-two fields in the cosmological gravitational wave collider.

papers.title: A Broadband Room-Temperature Design for the Einstein Telescope
papers.abstract: The unique underground location of the Einstein Telescope (ET) is expected to substantially suppress seismic and gravity-gradient noise, providing a favorable environment for gravitational-wave detection at low frequencies compared with surface-based observatories. The baseline ET design aims to achieve broadband sensitivity through a xylophone configuration, in which separate cryogenic and room-temperature interferometers are optimised for low- and high-frequency gravitational-wave detection. However, achieving the target low-frequency sensitivity introduces substantial technical complexity caused by vertical suspension thermal noise, vibrations of the cryocooler, and detuned optical configuration. In this paper, we demonstrate an alternative, entirely room-temperature, fully resonant, single-interferometer architecture that addresses these challenges and achieves broadband sensitivity superior to that of the conventional ET xylophone configuration. Using mature fused-silica suspension technology, recent advances in optical coatings, and novel inertial isolation, we show that 4-m-long fused-silica fibres can meet the required suspension thermal-noise performance. We further demonstrate that vibrations, optical rigidity, and quantum back-action noise can be controlled through appropriate design of the interferometer, test mass suspensions, optical seismometers, and quantum states.

papers.title: Searches for coincident Gravitational Waves and High-Energy Neutrinos from the KM3NeT and ANTARES telescopes during O3
papers.abstract: Various models predict that gravitational-wave sources produce high-energy neutrinos. Among them are compact binary coalescences with at least one neutron star, but also core-collapse supernovae or accretion disk instabilities. Two different analyses are presented, combining data from the LIGO and Virgo gravitational-wave detectors with those from the ANTARES and ORCA neutrino telescopes observed during the third observing run of LIGO-Virgo. In the first analysis, selected high-energy neutrino candidates were used as triggers to search for gravitational-wave candidates. In the second analysis, a search was conducted for potential spatial and temporal coincidences between subthreshold high-energy neutrino candidate events and subthreshold gravitational-wave candidates emitted by compact binary coalescence systems. In both searches, no significant coincidences were found. Upper limits on the rate of sources emitting both high-energy neutrinos and gravitational waves are presented. In particular, with the joint search, a joint source rate density upper limit of $8.8\times10^2~\mathrm{ Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ was found for a typical binary neutron star coalescence with a GW emitted energy of $10^{-1}~\rm M_\odot c^2$ and an isotropic energy emitted in neutrinos of $10^{51}~$erg.

papers.title: Orientation-dependent sensitivity of the all-sky all-frequency gravitational-wave radiometer search to continuous-wave sources
papers.abstract: The all-sky all-frequency (ASAF) gravitational-wave radiometer search cross-correlates the data of two detectors with equal weight on the $+$ and $\times$ tensor polarizations. This is optimal for an unpolarized stochastic background, but not for continuous-wave (CW) sources, whose polarization depends on the inclination angle $ι$ and the polarization angle $ψ$. Unless the source is seen face-on, the search measures less power than a face-on source with the same intrinsic amplitude, and underestimates its strength. The ratio of the two powers, the projection factor $μ^2(ι,ψ)$, is known from earlier radiometer studies. We show how $μ^2$ enters the ASAF statistic, derive its exact dependence on $ψ$, and prove that its average over orientations is exactly $2/5$, independent of sky position, baseline geometry, noise weighting, and frequency. We apply the formalism to four simulated pulsar signals at four sky positions, with polarization from circular to nearly linear, injected into the LIGO detectors during the second observing run (O2). A nearly edge-on injection is measured with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5.20$, below the threshold of $6.19$, while the same signal seen face-on would have an SNR of $31.1 \pm 6.0$. Bayesian upper limits on the strain amplitude $h_0$, marginalized over orientation and calibration uncertainty, are $2.7$ to $2.9$ times the face-on values. For the $505$ sub-threshold candidates of the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run (O4a), the upper limits increase by a factor of $2.5$ to $2.9$, and a source of the same strength would reach threshold only when inclined by less than $34.7^{\circ}$ to $50.3^{\circ}$ from face-on. The measured SNR and the significance of every candidate are unchanged.

papers.title: How general relativity stacks up: Testing gravity by coherently combining gravitational-wave observations
papers.abstract: A core mission of gravitational-wave astronomy is to test general relativity (GR) in the high-curvature, high-velocity regime. The field has already seen significant progress in this space, though a remaining challenge is how to combine data from a population of binary mergers. This can both boost the significance of potential GR violations, and develop a phenomenological picture of how deviations manifest in different mergers. We propose a framework to coherently combine gravitational-wave measurements to build a population-level test of physics beyond GR. We assume that deviations from GR are (i) strongest near the merger, (ii) vary smoothly with the total mass of the binary, and (iii) are most prominent in the $\ell=|m|=2$ mode. While these assumptions do not describe every possible deviation of GR, they provide us with a plausible starting point upon which a more general framework can be built. We apply our framework to 28 high signal-to-noise ratio binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, finding no evidence for deviations from GR. Our framework allows one to show how deviations could vary as a function of total mass of the system. We argue that such a reconstruction can be used to convincingly distinguish between systematic waveform errors and genuine GR violations.

papers.title: Parity-odd CMB Correlations induced by a Chiral Gravitational Wave Background
